title: Hook
text: What happens to information when it falls into a black hole? For decades, that single question troubled modern physics.
nxt: Imagine dropping an encyclopedia across the event horizon, the point of no return. Is the knowledge inside gone forever?

title: The Rule
text: Quantum theory has a strict rule: information is never truly destroyed.
nxt: In principle, the complete state of a system today determines its past and its future. So a black hole should not be able to erase a book.

title: The Glow
text: Then, in nineteen seventy-four, Stephen Hawking showed that black holes are not perfectly black.
nxt: They emit a faint thermal glow, now called Hawking radiation.

title: The Glow

nxt: For a black hole with the mass of our Sun, it is only about sixty billionths of a degree above absolute zero.

title: The Paradox
text: The glow carries energy away, so in theory the black hole shrinks and evaporates.
nxt: But the radiation looks purely thermal, a random glow that does not carry the contents of the book. Where did the information go?

title: A Bet in Dublin
text: Physicists split into camps. In the nineteen nineties, Hawking and Kip Thorne bet John Preskill that black holes destroy information.
nxt: In July two thousand four, at a conference in Dublin, Hawking conceded, and gave Preskill a baseball encyclopedia as the prize.

title: A Boundary Idea
text: Many physicists had already been persuaded by a different idea.
nxt: In nineteen ninety-seven, Juan Maldacena proposed that gravity in a certain kind of space is equivalent to a quantum theory on its boundary.

title: A Boundary Idea
text: In nineteen ninety-seven, Juan Maldacena proposed that gravity in a certain kind of space is equivalent to a quantum theory on its boundary.
prev: Many physicists had already been persuaded by a different idea.
nxt: Because the boundary theory obeys the usual quantum rules, information cannot be lost there. If the two descriptions truly match, it cannot be lost in the black hole either.

title: Outro
text: Maldacena's proposal is still a conjecture, and the space in his example is not our universe.
nxt: But the paradox pushed physicists toward a startling suspicion: space itself might emerge from quantum information.
